investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully consumed, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, no VM was provisioned, and the eval runner never wrote any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a complete contract violation.
investigation.rootCause: The production Kubernetes cluster has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm peer-pod VM slots. Of the 6 nodes in the cluster, only 2 carry this resource and both report "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" at scheduling time. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the two eligible nodes. As a result, every remote agent pod submitted during this eval window was stuck Unschedulable for ~144–146 seconds before the probe timed out, and no agent lifecycle evidence was ever produced. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion: the two peer-pod-capable nodes have no remaining VM slots, so any new remote agent pod is immediately Unschedulable. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message) and reproduced identically across all three sibling checks.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 peer-pod nodes satisfy, meaning the effective scheduling pool is already constrained to those 2 nodes before capacity is even considered.

Tertiary — leaked or stuck peer-pod VMs consuming slots: previously created remote agent VMs may not have been cleaned up, exhausting the finite kata.peerpods.io/vm quota on the two eligible nodes. The withCleanup wrapper in the runner (run-status-probes.mjs line 1883) is intended to handle cleanup, but a prior failed or interrupted run could have left VMs allocated.
Out-of-scope hypothesis — eval infrastructure misconfiguration: no evidence supports this; the scheduler message is a real Kubernetes API response, not a runner-side error.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately inspect the two kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes in the production cluster to determine current VM slot utilization and identify any leaked or stuck peer-pod VMs from prior eval or user runs.
If leaked VMs are found, clean them up through the appropriate cluster or swarm management interface to free kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and allow new remote agent pods to schedule.

If the cluster is at its hard VM capacity ceiling (no leaked VMs, all slots legitimately in use), escalate to the infrastructure team to evaluate expanding peer-pod node capacity or increasing the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota.

Review the remote agent pod's node affinity/selector configuration to confirm it is intentionally restricted to the 2 peer-pod nodes and that no recent change inadvertently narrowed the eligible node pool further.

After capacity is restored, re-run the full remote-agents eval suite (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) to confirm all checks pass and evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are present.

Consider adding a pre-flight capacity check to the eval runner that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm availability before attempting agent creation, so future capacity exhaustion produces a more actionable SKIP or WARN rather than a timeout-driven FAIL.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe on the two peer-pod nodes showed available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (allocatable > 0 free slots), the exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and a different scheduling or quota misconfiguration would need to be investigated.
If the remote-agent-create probe succeeded on an immediate re-run with no infrastructure changes, it would suggest a transient scheduling race rather than sustained capacity exhaustion.
If only one of the three sibling checks failed while the others passed, a shared capacity exhaustion would be less likely and a check-specific configuration issue would be more likely.

If the pod spec's node affinity/selector was recently changed to restrict scheduling to fewer nodes, that change (not capacity exhaustion) could be the primary cause — but no such change appears in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges.
If leaked VMs were found and cleaned up and the checks immediately passed, that would confirm the leaked-VM hypothesis over a hard capacity ceiling.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check (e.g., remote-agent-capacity) that queries the Kubernetes API for kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. capacity on peer-pod nodes and warns when free slots fall below a minimum threshold, catching exhaustion before agent creation attempts fail.

Add a VM slot leak detection eval that enumerates all active kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations and cross-references them against known live agent records, alerting when orphaned allocations are detected.

Add a post-cleanup verification step to the remote-agent-create probe that confirms the withCleanup wrapper successfully released the VM slot after each eval run, preventing eval-induced slot leakage.
Consider a canary eval that runs remote-agent-create on a non-production environment with a known-available peer-pod node to distinguish infrastructure capacity issues from API or runner regressions.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-06T14:27–14:32Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned an agent, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was written, causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm peer-pod VM slots across the 2 eligible nodes (0/2 available), and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. As a result, every attempt to schedule a remote agent pod during the eval window was rejected as Unschedulable with no preemption path available. The eval runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1905) calls createAgent with type "remote", which requires a kata peer-pod VM; that call timed out after ~144–146 seconds, preventing any evidence from being collected and causing all three remote-agents checks to fail. This is an infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents VM scheduling layer, not a code regression. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the eval.

With no schedulable node available and preemption unable to help (no lower-priority victims found), the pod remained in Pending/Unschedulable state for ~146 seconds until the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure, not an application code failure. No evidence of a user-facing production incident is present in the packet; this is an eval-observed failure scoped to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully consumed, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, no VM was provisioned, and the eval runner never wrote any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a complete contract violation.
investigations.rootCause: The production Kubernetes cluster has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm peer-pod VM slots. Of the 6 nodes in the cluster, only 2 carry this resource and both report "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" at scheduling time. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the two eligible nodes. As a result, every remote agent pod submitted during this eval window was stuck Unschedulable for ~144–146 seconds before the probe timed out, and no agent lifecycle evidence was ever produced. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion: the two peer-pod-capable nodes have no remaining VM slots, so any new remote agent pod is immediately Unschedulable. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message) and reproduced identically across all three sibling checks.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 peer-pod nodes satisfy, meaning the effective scheduling pool is already constrained to those 2 nodes before capacity is even considered.

Tertiary — leaked or stuck peer-pod VMs consuming slots: previously created remote agent VMs may not have been cleaned up, exhausting the finite kata.peerpods.io/vm quota on the two eligible nodes. The withCleanup wrapper in the runner (run-status-probes.mjs line 1883) is intended to handle cleanup, but a prior failed or interrupted run could have left VMs allocated.
Out-of-scope hypothesis — eval infrastructure misconfiguration: no evidence supports this; the scheduler message is a real Kubernetes API response, not a runner-side error.

Add a post-cleanup verification step to the remote-agent-create probe that confirms the withCleanup wrapper successfully released the VM slot after each eval run, preventing eval-induced slot leakage.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Failing
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-06T14:27–14:32Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the requested pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never started, the eval runner never received any response evidence, leaving all 5 required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent and the message assertion unverifiable.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (0 allocatable slots remaining), and the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. With no schedulable node available and preemption unable to help (no lower-priority victims found), the pod remained in Pending/Unschedulable state for ~146 seconds until the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure, not an application code failure. No evidence of a user-facing production incident is present in the packet; this is an eval-observed failure scoped to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) immediately after acquiring orgId — pod scheduling is the first infrastructure dependency; failure here blocks all downstream evidence collection.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189: remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false with outageLatencyMs=420000; the observed latencyMs=151847 is well under the outage threshold, so the failure is scheduling-driven, not a latency breach.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhaustion: the 2 nodes that carry this resource have zero remaining allocatable VM slots, preventing any new remote-agent pod from being scheduled. All three checks hit this condition independently within a ~5-minute window.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes satisfy, so the pool of eligible nodes is structurally limited to those 2, and both are already at capacity.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning or resource leak: a prior remote-agent pod (from an earlier eval run or a user workload) may not have been cleaned up, holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and leaving none available for the eval probes. The withCleanup wrapper in the runner (run-status-probes.mjs line 1916) is designed to release resources, but if a prior run crashed before cleanup, slots could remain occupied.

Lower confidence — transient capacity spike: a burst of concurrent remote-agent workloads from other sources temporarily exhausted the 2-node kata.peerpods.io/vm pool at the time of the eval run, and capacity may have recovered since.

Audit currently running and recently terminated remote-agent pods for any that are stuck in Terminating or Running state and holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without a corresponding active eval run — force-delete any leaked pods if found.

If capacity is genuinely exhausted by legitimate workloads, evaluate whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool needs to be scaled up (add nodes or increase per-node VM slot limits) to support concurrent eval probes alongside production workloads.

Review the node affinity/selector configuration on the remote-agent pod spec to confirm it is intentionally restricted to the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes and that no additional nodes could be made eligible.

Re-run all three remote-agent eval checks after any remediation to confirm recovery and that all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are populated and the message assertion ('hello from aura') passes.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity > 0 on both eligible nodes at the time of the failure, the exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different scheduling misconfiguration would need to be investigated.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeds and returns all 5 required evidence fields, the failure was a transient capacity spike rather than a persistent exhaustion or misconfiguration.

If the pod spec's node affinity/selector is found to match more than 2 nodes in the cluster, the structural pool-limitation hypothesis would be disproved and the root cause would be solely kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion.

If no remote-agent pods are found in Running or Terminating state holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, the resource-leak hypothesis would be disproved and the cause would be genuine capacity exhaustion from legitimate workloads.

If the local-agent-runtime or local-agent-create checks (which do not use kata.peerpods.io/vm) also failed at the same time, a broader cluster or API failure would need to be considered rather than a kata.peerpods.io/vm-specific issue.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity across all eligible nodes before attempting remote-agent pod creation, and fails fast with a descriptive capacity-exhaustion message rather than waiting for the scheduler timeout.

Add a resource-leak detection eval that lists remote-agent pods older than a configurable TTL (e.g., 10 minutes) and flags any that are still Running or Terminating, to catch withCleanup failures before they exhaust the VM slot pool.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., >= 2), alerting if the eligible pool shrinks unexpectedly.

Consider a canary eval that runs a lightweight no-op remote-agent pod scheduling dry-run (using --dry-run=server if supported) to detect Unschedulable conditions without consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots.
